component.name: Sable
component.summary: Lightweight raster painting with pen pressure

description.p: Sable is a small raster painting application for Linux, aimed at artists who want to open a program, sketch, and close it again. It starts in well under a second, presents a small interface, and runs on ordinary hardware with no discrete GPU.

Compositing happens on the CPU and the canvas is stored as sparse tiles, so memory follows the painted area rather than the canvas size. The event loop blocks when nobody is drawing, so an idle window costs nothing.

ul.li: Graphics tablet support with adjustable pressure curves and a stabilizer
Layers with blend modes, clipping and groups
Pencil, opaque, airbrush, marker, watercolour and smudge brushes
Projects saved as an inspectable ZIP of PNG tiles
Crash recovery that never overwrites your own files
Every action reachable from the keyboard, and every binding reassignable

description.p: Sable has no screen-reader support: its interface toolkit provides no AT-SPI integration. Full keyboard operability and interface scaling are offered in its place. This is a known limitation, recorded deliberately.

The brush ring follows the stylus. It was drawn where the interface toolkit believed the mouse to be, and while an artist hovers with a pen that toolkit falls back to polling the desktop cursor — so the ring sat wherever the mouse had been left, hundreds of pixels from the mark being made.

Alt and a tap samples the canvas with a stylus, as it always has with a mouse; the pen path never looked at the modifier. Picking a colour also has a binding of its own now, I by default, which needs no button held down.

The pointer now says which tool is in hand: a grab for the hand tool and for panning, a move or a diagonal resize over the transform box and its corners, and nothing at all inside the brush ring, which was drawn with an arrow sitting in the middle of the pixel being aimed at. The ring also follows a stylus while hovering, rather than staying where the mouse was left.

A tool options bar along the top, where Photoshop and Clip Studio both put one: whatever the tool in hand can be set to, and a line saying how to work it. Select and Transform in particular are no longer a guess.

Transform is a box on the canvas now. Drag inside it to move the selection, a corner to scale, Enter to apply and Escape to cancel, with the result live on the canvas rather than described by three number widgets.
A hand tool for panning, layer thumbnails so a layer can be recognised rather than read, and a fix for the previous drawing flickering up for a frame when a tab is opened.

A stylus can now work the interface. Sable turns SDL's synthetic mouse events off so that a stroke is never painted twice, which also left the interface unable to see a pen at all: hovering a panel did nothing and buttons needed a mouse. The pen's position and tip are now handed to the interface directly, and still reach the canvas only once.

The bucket, fill, gradient and clear tools write a layer mask when Paint on mask is on, instead of being held back. A gradient down a mask is how a layer is faded out, which is most of the reason to want one.

New artists open on a seven-step walkthrough, reachable again from Help or F1. The key map and the tablet pages moved to a Help menu, an untouched canvas says how to start, and the canvas is centred in the window rather than left in a corner.

Pen pressure now reaches the first dab of a stroke. SDL reports a frame's pressure after the position it belongs to, so every stroke opened at the pressure of the frame before it — nothing at all on a freshly started application. A pen whose pressure the driver never reports is treated as full pressure rather than none.

Layer masks, painted with the ordinary brushes. Linear and radial gradients. Brush shapes and paper texture, so the presets make different marks rather than the same mark at different settings. Several drawings open at once as tabs, each with its own zoom and undo history. Selections that can be kept by name, taken from a layer or a mask, and combined without losing a soft edge. Linework curves that close, move as a whole and recolour after the fact. ICC colour management, so a tagged file keeps the colours it was made with.
Fixes canvas overlays drawing outside the canvas. Ruler guides, the selection outline and the brush cursor could paint over the docked panels and out of the window.

Optional GPU painting and compositing, 16-bit colour, linework layers, text layers, lasso and magic wand selection, perspective and symmetry rulers, canvas rotation, and import and export of PSD, OpenRaster and Krita files.
